title: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

sense.text:
This class is on the repercussions of sin, because it seems we have lost the fear of the Most High God; cases of adultery keep going on week after week.

“There were present at that season some that told him of the Galileans, whose blood Pilate had mingled with their sacrifices.” Pilate had killed some Israelites while they were attempting to sacrifice to the Lord: murdering Israelites that sacrificed. Pilate was not a good guy. He is the same man who said he found no fault with Christ, and Christians use that to say Pilate was decent. Read this verse and see what he did.

“Suppose ye that these Galileans were sinners above all the Galileans, because they suffered such things?” The thought back then is the thought now: when people die, especially in a horrible way, we say they must have been some sinners, wicked as hell.

“I tell you, Nay.” Christ said no, they were not the worst sinners above all. “But, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.” He is speaking to the disciples and his other followers. It is the same when people get shot down in the streets today; back then they did not have guns, they used literal swords, but it is the same example. Except we repent, we shall all likewise perish.

“Those eighteen, upon whom the tower in Siloam fell, and slew them, think ye that they were sinners above all men that dwelt in Jerusalem?” It is like when the World Trade towers collapsed and people said they must have been the most wicked. Christ said “Nay”: they were not the worst sinners. “But, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.” Except we repent, we can die the same way.

“Fear not the sentence of death, remember them that have been before thee, and that come after; for this is the sentence of the Lord over all flesh.” Death is the sentence from the Lord over all flesh. Everybody is destined to die; this physical body is destined to perish.

“And why art thou against the pleasure of the most High?” That is heavy. “There is no inquisition in the grave”: when you die there is no inquisition, no questioning, “whether thou have lived ten, or an hundred, or a thousand years.” When we die, we are at rest.

precepts.why:
Job is the precept that there is no inquisition in the grave. Job was catching so much hell that he said “Why died I not from the womb? why did I not give up the ghost when I came out of the belly?” Why didn’t I die as a baby? His kids got put to death, he lost all his businesses, he got sick, all kinds of plagues were on his flesh, and his wife was a nag getting on his nerves.

“Why did the knees prevent me? or why the breasts that I should suck?” The knees are the mother rocking a baby on her knees to keep it up and about. “For now should I have lain still and been quiet, I should have slept: then had I been at rest”, “with kings and counsellors of the earth”, “or with princes that had gold, who filled their houses with silver”, “or as an hidden untimely birth”: a still birth, “as infants which never saw light.”

“There the wicked cease from troubling; and there the weary be at rest. There the prisoners rest together; they hear not the voice of the oppressor.” The prisoners are our people, at rest together in death. “The small and great are there”, in the grave, at rest, “and the servant is free from his master.”

So when we die, brothers and sisters, we are all at rest, whether you are righteous or you are wicked as hell.

“The righteous perisheth, and no man layeth it to heart”, and Isaiah says “the righteous is taken away from the evil to come.” When he dies “He shall enter into peace: they shall rest in their beds”: the chambers of rest.

Then: “each one walking in his uprightness.” When the righteous die they are walking in their uprightness, walking before the Lord. They are not really dead. The wicked are at rest, they sleep, but the righteous are up, talking before the Lord.

This shows the righteous more. At the fifth seal John saw “under the altar the souls of them that were slain for the word of God, and for the testimony which they held.” Remember, they are dead, yet “they cried with a loud voice, saying, How long, O Lord, holy and true, dost thou not judge and avenge our blood on them that dwell on the earth?”

So not only are they walking, they are talking to the Lord, asking for vengeance. We have to get that in our minds and understand what death is and what it is not.

sense.text:
The Christian church is insane when it comes to dying.

“The days of visitation are come, the days of recompence are come; Israel shall know it”: we Israelites shall know it by reading the scriptures. “The prophet is a fool”: the prophets are these preachers out here, and you are going to find out they are fools. “The spiritual man is mad”: the spiritual men out here are insane, crazy, psychologically defective. “For the multitude of thine iniquity”: for the multitude of sins.

“And the great hatred”: these preachers and ministers have a great hatred against the laws of God, a hatred against doing what the Bible says. That is why, when brothers sit down with church ministers, the ministers tend to say, let’s not read out of the Bible, let’s just talk. That is the great hatred against the word of God. They hate the scriptures.

Here are the various ways hell is used in the Bible. Write this down: hell is used in the context of the grave.

“For thou wilt not leave my soul in hell; neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption.” Corruption is when the worms eat you up and you are being corroded in the ground. So he uses the grave as hell. Hell is called the grave.

Write this down: hell is also used as a low state of being, oppression and slavery.

“Because ye have said, We have made a covenant with death, and with hell are we at agreement; when the overflowing scourge shall pass through, it shall not come unto us: for we have made lies our refuge, and under falsehood have we hid ourselves.” Our leaders, our rulers, made a covenant with death and hell.

precepts.why: “The sorrows of death compassed me, and the pains of hell gat hold upon me: I found trouble and sorrow.” See how he uses hell in this context. He speaks of the sorrows of death, but he ain’t dead yet. The pains of hell are great pain, like the prophet Job was in: that is called hell.

Put this one next to Isaiah 28:15. “Whose possessors slay them, and hold themselves not guilty”: the possessors are the owners. That is slavery: they kill us and hold themselves not guilty.

“And they that sell them say, Blessed be the Lord; for I am rich”: they profited, they made money off selling us in slavery. “And their own shepherds pity them not.” Our shepherds are our rulers, the leaders of our people that made a covenant with death and hell.

“Therefore my people are gone into captivity, because they have no knowledge: and their honourable men are famished, and their multitude dried up with thirst. Therefore hell hath enlarged herself, and opened her mouth without measure.” What is this hell talking about? Verse 13 tells you: captivity. Here Isaiah uses the term hell for captivity.

“And their glory, and their multitude, and their pomp, and he that rejoiceth, shall descend into it”: descend into captivity.

sense.text:
Another reference for hell. Write this down: damnation. This is the one many Israelite camps don’t want to discuss.

“Ye serpents, ye generation of vipers, how can ye escape the damnation of hell?” The damnation of hell. Now we get into what this hell is talking about.

“Measure thou the time diligently in itself: and when thou seest part of the signs past, which I have told thee before, Then shalt thou understand, that it is the very same time, wherein the Highest will begin to visit the world which he made.” The Highest visiting the world he made is him sending his angels.

“Therefore when there shall be seen earthquakes and uproars of the people in the world.” Are we seeing earthquakes in the world today? Yes. Do we see uproars of the people? Yes. That is why there is no time for people that don’t believe the Bible. The Bible speaks and we are seeing it in real time. If you ain’t got your head on Atlanta housewives, you know what’s going on.

So when we see these things happening, we ain’t got time to play with these brothers and sisters who want to be swallowed up in all that.

“Then shalt thou well understand, that the most High spake of those things from the days that were before thee, even from the beginning.” “For like as all that is made in the world hath a beginning and an end, and the end is manifest: Even so the times also of the Highest have plain beginnings in wonder and powerful works, and endings in effects and signs.” We are seeing the effects and signs of what was prophesied.

“And every one that shall be saved, and shall be able to escape by his works, and by faith, whereby ye have believed.” Listen good: this is what we all want. We want to be able to escape by our works, keeping the commandments, and by faith in Christ.

“Shall be preserved from the said perils”: if we have faith in Christ and works, keeping the commandments, we shall be preserved from the said perils, from the destruction to come. “And shall see my salvation in my land”: we shall see the Lord’s salvation in his land, and that is Israel, “and within my borders.” We want to see the resurrection of Jerusalem, the resurrection of the twelve tribes of Israel.

“For I have sanctified them for me from the beginning”: he sanctified us, he chose us from the beginning of the world.

“Then shall they be in pitiful case, which now have abused my ways.” To abuse his ways means they got the Bible, they got the word of the Lord, but they are not obeying what it says. They are doing their own thing.

These are your Christian pastors abusing God’s ways. Pastor Michael Todd, in a sermon about receiving vision from God, saying ‘it might get nasty’: filth, some sodomy stuff, some homo stuff. Pastor Noel Jones and the preachers of LA in a preach-off, thirty seconds each about life not being a reality show: no scripture, just abusing the Lord’s ways, and Christian black women love that stuff. A preacher said his sermon was about Jonah and the whale swallowing Jonah, and started off ‘come out the closet’: that has nothing to do with Jonah. This devil knows what he is doing; he confessed what he is doing. That is more examples of abusing God’s ways.

“And they that have cast them away despitefully shall dwell in torments.” What is the word in this verse for damnation? Torments. Them guys are going to dwell in torments: that is the damnation.

“For such as in their life have received benefits, and have not known me.” The benefits are money: money, money, money. The ten richest pastors in Africa, the preachers of LA. They got money, they got clout, fame and fortune and women. Notice what comes with the benefits: not knowing the Lord. These pastors received benefits, and have not known him.

“And they that have loathed my law”: loathed means hated. You that have hated God’s law. “While they had yet liberty”: that is what the church blitz is all about. They have liberty to repent, and our job is to sit down with them and try to win them over.

“And, when as yet place of repentance was open unto them”: that is when the brothers go in front of the churches and hand out flyers to them; that is the place of repentance. “Understood not, but despised it”: hated it.

“The same must know it after death by pain.” Put it with the bottom of verse 9, “shall dwell in torments”: the torments are the pain after death. Highlight that in your Bible and your notebook. But we just read in Job that everybody is at rest when they die. So what is the torment, what is the pain after death? It is the damnation of hell. Nobody wants to talk about that.

precepts.why: What are the works? Revelation 14:12 tells you it is faith and works: “Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus.” The works are keeping the commandments, and the faith is faith in Christ. That is how everyone that shall be saved shall escape.

What does “I have sanctified them for me from the beginning” mean? “God hath from the beginning chosen you to salvation”: he has chosen us from the beginning, talking about Genesis, “through sanctification of the Spirit and belief of the truth.”

“And now when I prepared the world, which was not yet made, even for them to dwell in that now live, no man spake against me.” In the beginning, before the earth was made, no man spake against him. “For then every one obeyed”: we were all there with him in the beginning, and then everyone obeyed.

“But now the manners of them which are created in this world that is made are corrupted by a perpetual seed, and by a law which is unsearchable rid themselves.” So the ones he sanctified from the beginning are the ones that were with him before the world was made.

“With all deceivableness of unrighteousness in them that perish”: them that perish are our people, “because they received not the love of the truth”, which is faith in Christ and keeping the commandments, “that they might be saved.”

“And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie: That they all might be damned.” What is that word? Damned. That is the same thing Christ said in Matthew 23:33. “Who believed not the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness”: that is them, these pastors. Their damnation is the torments of 2 Esdras 9:9.

Keys of hell and death. Christ is speaking: “I am he that liveth, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore, Amen; and have the keys of hell and of death.” Wait a minute: Christ says he has the keys of hell and death.

Hell in the context of the grave is the sentence on all flesh; everybody dies, so this is not talking about that. Sorrow, trouble, oppression and slavery have been going on from the beginning, so it is not talking about that either. This hell, this death, is the damnation we read about in Matthew 23. It is not a car crash. This death and hell is the torment; it is what they shall know “after death by pain.”

Back to it one more time: “Ye serpents, ye generation of vipers, how can ye escape the damnation of hell?” The damnation of hell. Christ is not talking about the grave, which is the sentence on all flesh. He is not talking about sorrow, captivity or trouble in the flesh. This is that torment, which many of our people don’t believe in.

“What I tell you in darkness”: what I told you in private, “that speak ye in light”: I want you to speak it openly before all the people. “And what ye hear in the ear”: what I’ve told you in your ear privately, “that preach ye upon the housetops”: go on the housetops and preach it loud to everybody. What he told us in parables, he wants us to make plain to the people. But in the same token he’s saying, what you going to say out there is going to get you killed.

“And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul”: he says that because what we preach in public will get us killed. “But rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.” In where? In hell. That’s the damnation.

Man can only kill the flesh, this body. Once this is gone your soul is still alive; the real you is alive. But Christ said, if you disobey, fear the Lord, that can kill not just your body but your soul too, in hell. That’s damnation, the pain after death.

“Are not two sparrows sold for a farthing? and one of them shall not fall on the ground without your Father.” A bird does not die without the Father’s consent, and he’s talking about us. “But the very hairs of your head are all numbered”: that’s how important you are, you Israelites; every hair on our head is numbered. “Fear ye not therefore, ye are of more value than many sparrows”: you’re more important than birds, brothers and sisters.

Go back to verse 28, fear not them which kill the body, then 32: “Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men”, that’s in fear of death, “him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.” If you ain’t afraid, he’s going to confess you before the heavenly Father.

“But whosoever shall deny me before men”, because you scared to die. You don’t want this flesh burned, your head cut off, to be stabbed, dragged behind a car, whiplashed, or tied by your arms and legs to horses and ripped apart. Christ said, “him will I also deny before my Father which is in heaven.” And guess what that is: damnation. Christ denying you is damnation.

“But he that sinneth against me wrongeth his own soul.” All you adulterers out there, listen good: you ain’t wronging us, you are wronging your own soul. He didn’t say you wrong your own body; he said you wrong your soul.

“All they that hate me love death.” What kind of death is that talking about? It ain’t talking about the death of your body, because he is talking about your soul. This is that damnation.

“For Moses truly said unto the fathers, A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me”: Moses prophesied about the coming Christ way back in Deuteronomy 18, and here they quote it. “Him shall ye hear in all things whatsoever he shall say unto you”: whatever Christ says, you better obey him.

“And it shall come to pass, that every soul”, every soul, “which will not hear that prophet”, you that reject the teachings of Christ and don’t want to hear what he said, “shall be destroyed from among the people.” That ain’t no regular death, because we read at the beginning of class that death is the sentence on all flesh; everybody physically dies. He is talking about a deeper death.

sense.text:
A parable that Christ gave us. “There was a certain rich man, which was clothed in purple and fine linen, and fared sumptuously every day”. The rich man who fared sumptuously is those ministers, those politicians, those Israelites who have received benefits: they got money, fame and fortune, and everybody loves them. This rich man does not represent Rome, and it does not represent the white man.

Remember what we read earlier: the rulers of our people have made a covenant with death and hell. They made an agreement with Rome, just like today these ministers have made an agreement with the United States of America: keep these people in sin, keep these people in lies, and as long as we get paid we good.
“And there was a certain beggar named Lazarus, which was laid at his gate, full of sores”. Lazarus represents the Israelites, the repentant Israelites.

“And desiring to be fed with the crumbs which fell from the rich man’s table”: our people want the crumbs that the leaders of our society have. That’s the welfare and all that, the low paying jobs. When they in Congress fighting for jobs, the jobs we getting are not jobs to be CEOs; we get jobs to be workers. The ministers say I’m going to go to Congress and fight for you, and you get a job, you get a job.

“Moreover the dogs came and licked his sores.” The dogs are the nations, and also these low-level preachers. The nations open up businesses, like the Chinese and the Italians, in poor communities, and take, take, take so that they can build their communities, but meanwhile we stay impoverished.

“And it came to pass, that the beggar died”: I gave you more than one death, and that’s death right there. He “was carried by the angels into Abraham’s bosom”: Abraham’s bosom is the covenant made with Abraham, the blessings we are going to inherit.

“The rich man also died”: the one that was in purple and fared sumptuously every day, he died, “and was buried”. This rich man represents all people that have benefits in this world. They die, and now they in the grave.

“And in hell he lift up his eyes, being in torments”. That hell is the torment. It’s the same torment we read in 2 Esdras 9, and it’s the same thing Christ said in Matthew 23:33 about damnation. He “seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom.”

“Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame.” Tormented in what? In this flame. This is what Christ said: fear him that can destroy both body and soul in hell.

It ain’t talking about, like the church say, the middle of the earth. It’s still another realm, another dimension; that’s what it’s going into.

“Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things”: what was the word we read in 2 Esdras 9? Benefits. “And likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted”, comforted in the bosom of Abraham, the kingdom, because that’s what it’s talking about, “and thou art tormented.” Now it’s your turn to be tormented. You thought you got away with that good life, but now you’re tormented.

I know what you’re thinking: I thought you read in Job we all at peace. Remember, Christ said he has the keys of hell and death.

“Between us and you there is a great gulf fixed: so that they which would pass from hence to you cannot; neither can they pass to us, that would come from thence.” That’s how you know it’s another realm, another dimension. This great gulf is another dimension, another realm. They couldn’t go to them and they can’t come to us, but they could see: Abraham and Lazarus could see the rich man in torment, but they could not reach one another.

“I pray thee therefore, father, that thou wouldest send him to my father’s house: For I have five brethren”. Look at the five brothers: they living good, they living lavish, they got women, they got fortune, they got wealth, they got it all. “That he may testify unto them, lest they also come into this place of torment.”

“They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.” That’s how you know this rich man ain’t Esau. It says they have Moses and the prophets: that’s about Israel. The Israelites got Moses and the prophets. Let them hear them: let them study their scriptures.
“Nay, father Abraham: but if one went unto them from the dead, they will repent.” That’s a lie. They never would repent.
“If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.” They won’t be persuaded if one rose from the dead, and Matthew 28 shows it.

precepts.why: We’re going to talk about the dogs for a second. “But against any of the children of Israel shall not a dog move his tongue, against man or beast: that ye may know how that the Lord doth put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel.” God is calling the Hamites dogs; the Lord is talking about the other nations.

Remember, this is the Greek woman: “Then came she and worshipped him, saying, Lord, help me.” “But he answered and said, It is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it to dogs.” To who? To dogs. Christ is calling the Greek woman a dog: not just her, her daughter, all her people. So the reference to dogs is the other nations.

But guess what, dogs is also talking about our people too, because our people also tend to take advantage of one another. Allegedly, in Atlanta, a brother did a whole campaign about people sending money, a Tulsa fund, like rebuilding Black Wall Street; they had a convention and raised a million dollars, and then the fund only had about seven hundred thousand dollars in it. That’s what happens.

“His watchmen are blind”: there’s a lot of watchmen, including these preachers in the hood with no education, unlearned preachers that mimic what they see the rich preachers do and open up little churches. “They are all ignorant, they are all dumb dogs”: notice, he’s calling them dogs. “They cannot bark”: they can’t prophesy, they can’t teach the word of God. “Sleeping, lying down, loving to slumber.”

This year you’re going to see a bunch of dumb dogs. These pastors are going to invite Republicans and Democrats, Joe Biden, Donald Trump, senators and congressmen, inside the church to convince black people to vote for them, and when they get in office they don’t do nothing for black people. Exactly. That’s the covenant: as long as they get paid, they don’t give a damn about the people.

“Yea, they are greedy dogs which can never have enough”: they always want give me, give me, give me. “And they are shepherds that cannot understand”: shepherds that cannot understand the word of God. That’s what we read in 2 Esdras 9: they have not known me. “They all look to their own way, every one for his gain”, his financial gain, “from his quarter”: his church.

“And was carried by the angels into Abraham’s bosom”: start at verse 5. “Neither shall thy name any more be called Abram, but thy name shall be Abraham; for a father of many nations have I made thee. And I will make thee exceeding fruitful, and I will make nations of thee, and kings shall come out of thee.”

“And I will establish my covenant between me and thee and thy seed after thee”: thy seed after thee is talking about Israel, “in their generations for an everlasting covenant, to be a God unto thee, and to thy seed after thee.” That covenant that was made with Abraham, that’s his bosom. We going to inherit all the blessings that were given to Abraham.

“And I will give unto thee, and to thy seed after thee, the land wherein thou art a stranger, all the land of Canaan, for an everlasting possession; and I will be their God.” That’s going to be the area of New Jerusalem; in fact Jerusalem is going to be larger than that.

Thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things: go right back to 2 Esdras 9. “Then shall they be in pitiful case, which now have abused my ways: and they that have cast them away despitefully shall dwell in torments. For such as in their life have received benefits, and have not known me”. It’s not saying anything different; it’s saying the same thing. The good things the rich man received in his lifetime are the benefits.

“And they that have loathed my law, while they had yet liberty, and, when as yet place of repentance was open unto them, understood not, but despised it; The same must know it after death by pain.” By what? By pain. So Christ is saying, now it’s your turn to be tormented.

“And it shall come to pass, that from one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me, saith the Lord”: this is talking about the kingdom, so we know the kingdom is set up at this time.

Here it come: “And they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me”: you broke the commandments, you rejected Christ. “For their worm shall not die”: their worm is their soul; their soul shall not die. “Neither shall their fire be quenched.”

So that’s in the kingdom, and like Abraham and Lazarus seeing the rich man across the gulf, they go forth and look upon them. When the kingdom is established, that’s why Christ said he has the keys to death and hell; when he returns, this is what he’s going to do.
They have Moses and the prophets: “For had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me: for he wrote of me. But if ye believe not his writings, how shall ye believe my words?”

He said if one went unto them from the dead they will repent. “Much people of the Jews therefore knew that he was there: and they came not for Jesus’ sake only, but that they might see Lazarus also, whom he had raised from the dead.” Christ had just raised Lazarus from the dead. “But the chief priests consulted that they might put Lazarus also to death”. You see how wicked these are? These are wicked as hell. One came back from the dead, and instead of repenting they wanted to kill him again.

If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded: “For had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me: for he wrote of me. But if ye believe not his writings, how shall ye believe my words?” That’s right.

Remember, Christ had just resurrected. “Behold, some of the watch came into the city, and shewed unto the chief priests all the things that were done”: the stone was moved away and Christ was gone, the body was gone. “And when they were assembled with the elders, and had taken counsel, they gave large money unto the soldiers, Saying, Say ye, His disciples came by night, and stole him away while we slept.”

They concocted a lie. When you read it, the angel came down, the guards got frightened and fled, the stone was moved away and Christ came out. But the elders said no, here’s some money, you’re going to say this lie. “And if this come to the governor’s ears, we will persuade him, and secure you.” That also puts more of a bounty on the apostles’ heads: you broke Pilate’s seal and went in there and stole a body, so we got to arrest these guys.

“So they took the money, and did as they were taught: and this saying is commonly reported among the Jews until this day.” One rose from the dead, and they were not persuaded.

sense.text:
I’m going through this because you got Israelites that teach you can be an adulterer, a thief, a liar, even a homo, and when you die you get the kingdom of heaven. Any of you men and women that believe that garbage?

“Whosoever shall offend one of these little ones that believe in me”: the little ones that believe are you men and women who have the faith of Christ and keep the commandments, the ones that keep the commandments of God and have the faith of Jesus. Christ said if you sin against these little ones, “it is better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and he were cast into the sea.” It’s better that you kill yourself; that’s what the Son of God said.

The offense is, let’s go worship other gods. Nobody’s literally going to say that, but they’re going to try to convince you to go back to Islam, go back to the Catholic church or the Baptist church, or get you into some sin to pull you out from keeping the commandments. That’s their goal, that’s their objective, whether it’s male or female.

“And if thy hand offend thee, cut it off”: it ain’t talking about cutting off your literal hand. Under Moses we literally had to kill our brother, our wife, our son, our daughter, our friend that enticed us; Christ ain’t telling us to literally kill nobody, he’s saying cut him off. That hand is your wife, that might be your son, your daughter, your best friend, your mama, your daddy.

“It is better for thee to enter into life maimed, than having two hands to go into hell”: to go where? Into hell, “into the fire that never shall be quenched”.

Nobody wants to talk about that. You’d rather stay close to your good friends. One sister left the truth to run behind a brother because he went to the gym and had all them muscles. They got married, and a month after that she saw text messages on his phone with another man calling him babe, boo, I love you, you so sexy. She asked him was he a homo and he beat her up. Now the sister says I want to come back: no, pump the brakes, you stay out there, you made your choice. Little did you know he wasn’t interested in you, you stupid black women.
“Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.” This is the same thing we read in Isaiah 66: their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched. The worm is the soul.

“And if thy foot offend thee, cut it off”: your foot might be your buddy, your friend, your mama, who carries you here and carries you there and entices you to sin, entices you to break God’s law, to go someplace else. “It is better for thee to enter halt into life, than having two feet to be cast into hell, into the fire that never shall be quenched: Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.” This is unquenchable fire; you ain’t blowing this fire out.

“And if thine eye offend thee, pluck it out”: that eye might be your wife, that eye might be your mother. “It is better for thee to enter into the kingdom of God with one eye”: it’s better that you enter the kingdom single, with no spouse, “than having two eyes to be cast into hell fire”.

Some of you men, you simps, you know your wife is a damn devil, but you want to hold on to her. Hold on to her then, and you going to get this judgment right here that we reading about. Just like the women: they know the man is no damn good, but they hold on, I got to have him.

“Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.” This is unquenchable fire, spiritual nuclear fire, God’s fire.
“For every one shall be salted with fire”.

precepts.why:
“Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.” This unquenchable fire is what we’ve been reading about all day. When Christ comes and destroys nations, he said, I’m going to cast some of y’all into the lake of fire immediately.

The fan is what makes the fire hotter; he’s going to turn it up.

“For, behold, the Lord will come with fire, and with his chariots like a whirlwind, to render his anger with fury, and his rebuke with flames of fire. For by fire and by his sword will the Lord plead with all flesh: and the slain of the Lord shall be many.” Christ going to do a whole lot of killing, a whole lot of killing.

sense.text: Watch what it says here: “But the rest of the dead lived not again until the thousand years were finished.” One third is going to inherit that kingdom, but what about the two thirds? The rest of the dead lived not again till the thousand years were finished. “This is the first resurrection.”

“Blessed and holy is he that hath part in the first resurrection”: that’s when that one third gets taken up. “On such the second death hath no power”: that second death, the lake of fire, has no power over them. “But they shall be priests of God and of Christ, and shall reign with him a thousand years.”

We’ve gone over this before. Satan is loosed “to deceive the nations which are in the four quarters of the earth, Gog and Magog, to gather them together to battle”, and they “compassed the camp of the saints about”: that’s Ezekiel chapter 38 and chapter 39. “And fire came down from God out of heaven, and devoured them.”

Pay closer attention to verse 10: “And the devil that deceived them was cast into the lake of fire and brimstone, where the beast and the false prophet are.” Stop: where the beast and the false prophet are. They’re already there. Remember, this is a thousand years later: they’re waiting on the rest. “And shall be tormented day and night for ever and ever.”

“And I saw a great white throne, and him that sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away”: so when Christ comes on the scene in his power and majesty, nobody got nothing to say. Everything shuts down. “And there was found no place for them.”

“And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God”: stand before Christ. “And the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works.”

“And the sea gave up the dead which were in it”: those that died in the sea, those spirits were raised up and resurrected. “And death and hell delivered up the dead which were in them”: those that were killed by war, the sword, famine, the beasts of the earth, and death, like disease. “And they were judged every man according to their works.”
“And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death.” So all is going to end. “And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.”

precepts.why:
“And it shall come to pass, that in all the land”: in what? In all the land. Is there an s there? No sir, ’cause it’s talking about Babylon the great: in all the land. “Saith the Lord, two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein. And I will bring the third part through the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and will try them as gold is tried: they shall call on my name, and I will hear them: I will say, It is my people: and they shall say, The Lord is my God.”

So one third is going to inherit that kingdom. But what about the two thirds? Go back to Revelation 20:5: “But the rest of the dead lived not again until the thousand years were finished.”

“For the Father judgeth no man”: God the Father judges no man, “but hath committed all judgment unto the Son.” You see that? Christ is going to do all the judging, brothers and sisters, not the Father. The Father’s just chilling; he’s sitting back, he’s letting his Son Christ do everything. So the dead stand before God: they stand before Christ.

Let me show you what the death and hell is. “And I looked, and behold a pale horse: and his name that sat on him was Death, and Hell followed with him. And power was given unto them over the fourth part of the earth, to kill with sword”: those that were killed with the sword, “and with hunger”: those that were killed with hunger, “and with death, and with the beasts of the earth.”

Go back to Revelation 20:13: “death and hell delivered up the dead which were in them.” So those that were killed by war, the sword, famine, the beasts of the earth, and death, like disease: death and hell deliver them up.

Revelation 21:7 and 8 again: “He that overcometh shall inherit all things; and I will be his God, and he shall be my son. But the fearful, and unbelieving, and the abominable, and murderers, and whoremongers, and sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone: which is the second death.” These are the ones not found written in the book of life.

Now the question might be, why doesn’t the Lord judge everybody at the same time when he returns? Why does he wait for a thousand years and then cast people into the lake of fire? How many people are on earth in 2023: about 8 billion, and that’s a rough estimate that Esau came up with. Why doesn’t he do it all at once? That’s the same thing Ezra asked.

“Go thy way to a woman with child, and ask of her when she hath fulfilled her nine months, if her womb may keep the birth any longer within her. Then said I, No, Lord, that can she not. And he said unto me, In the grave the chambers of souls are like the womb of a woman.” Stop, look at that: in the grave the chambers of souls are like the womb of a woman. Meaning what? Those souls that were in the grave come back, just like the woman gives birth: the dead, they come back. But guess what: the group that goes into the lake of fire, they don’t come back. They stay right there.

“For like as a woman that travaileth maketh haste to escape the necessity of the travail: even so do these places haste to deliver those things that are committed unto them.” They haste to give those spirits back up, to have them come back. That’s the sea and death and hell giving up the dead which were in them.

“And what shall they do that have been before me”: what shall those souls do that have been before me? There are generations of people that were before Ezra; he’s asking, what about them? “Or we that be now”: ’cause sometimes we think that everybody on the planet now, that’s everybody. This is not everybody; there are generations before us, way before us. “Or they that shall come after us?” So Ezra said you have nations of men before us, the generation that’s currently living, and generations after us: what about those three groups?

“I will liken my judgment unto a ring: like as there is no slackness of the last, even so there is no swiftness of the first.” So judgment is like a steady rotation: everybody got to get it, everybody gets it.

“Couldest thou not make those that have been made, and be now, and that are for to come, at once”, do everything at once, “that thou mightest shew thy judgment the sooner? Then answered he me, and said, The creature may not haste above the maker; neither may the world hold them at once that shall be created therein.” The angel said the planet can’t hold everybody at one time.

That’s why, when we read, he said this group I’m casting into the lake of fire, this other group I’m just going to kill y’all, but then a thousand years later, now I’m going to get this group here. Everything can’t be done at once; you can’t get them all at once. Ain’t nobody on the planet teaching this, and it’s crystal clear. The beast and the false prophet are already there waiting, so there’s a group out of every generation that he’s putting there, and when another group comes he’s going to add them to it, until all of the generations are taken care of, in that lake of fire forever.

sense.text: “For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive. But every man in his own order: Christ the firstfruits; afterward they that are Christ’s at his coming.” So notice: every man in his own order. There’s no such thing as equality; everyone’s going to be in their order.

“Then cometh the end, when he shall have delivered up the kingdom to God, even the Father; when he shall have put down all rule and all authority and power”: when Christ puts down all rule and all authority and power, when Christ subdues everything on the planet.
“For he must reign”: Christ must reign, “till he hath put all enemies under his feet.”
“The last enemy that shall be destroyed is death”: that’s what we just read in Revelation 20, death and hell cast into the lake of fire.

“For he hath put all things under his feet”: he, the Father, put all things under Christ’s feet. “But when he saith all things are put under him”, under Christ, “it is manifest that he is excepted”: it is manifest that the Father is excepted. The Father is not being subject under Christ; he is the one “which did put all things under him”.

“And when all things shall be subdued unto him, then shall the Son also himself be subject unto him that put all things under him, that God may be all in all.” When Christ subdues everything, then he’s going to submit everything to the Father. That’s why he said what we read earlier: the Father judges no man, but has committed all judgment to the Son.

Christ is the God of this earth. Like I said in John 1, people get all discombobulated: why I say Christ is God? Because he created everything. We read that; we have many classes on that. So once Christ subdues everything, everything submits to his Father, like a son would do: the Son goes out, conquers everything, and brings all the rewards to the Father.
“Let us therefore, as many as be perfect”: as many as walk in the spirit, “be thus minded: and if in any thing ye be otherwise minded, God shall reveal even this unto you.”

“Nevertheless, whereto we have already attained”: we got this knowledge, this understanding. “Let us walk by the same rule”: let all of us, brothers and sisters, walk by the same rule; that’s God’s laws. “Let us mind the same thing.”

“Brethren, be followers together of me, and mark them which walk so”: he said mark those, as you have us for an example. Watch those who are keeping the commandments, take good note of them: those men, those women following the example.

“For many walk, of whom I have told you often, and now tell you even weeping, that they are the enemies of the cross of Christ.” Those are your adulterers, your liars, your thieves, your drug users, drug abusers, your haters, your child molesters. And some of them are sitting in here among us; some of them are online.

“Whose end is destruction”, like we read earlier. During this time he’s referring to the scribes and Pharisees and them, ’cause them was wicked as hell. “Whose God is their belly”: it’s always give me, what can I get from this, give me, give me, all about me. “And whose glory is in their shame, who mind earthly things”: those men, those women mind earthly things.

“For our conversation is in heaven”: our talk, our conversation, should be in heaven; our conversation should be in this Bible. Now I know it ain’t easy to always talk about the scriptures, but guess what, we got to train ourselves for that, just like you have trained yourself to talk about sports stats. Some of y’all know every stat, and I’m like, what the hell are you talking about? He scored this, he scored that, he was born on this: what the hell, who gives a damn about that?

“We look for the Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ”: that’s what we look for.

“Who shall change our vile body”: all our bodies are vile. These bodies we got are broken and sickly, filled with pestilence, disease, sickness, and destined to die to corruption. “That it may be fashioned like unto his glorious body”: that celestial, that God body, is what we want. “According to the working whereby he is able even to subdue all things unto himself”: Christ is going to subdue all things unto himself.

“But thou, Israel, art my servant”: thou Israel, you my servant, “Jacob whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraham my friend.” Abraham our friend: just like we read about Lazarus, taken into the bosom of Abraham. God called Abraham his friend; he didn’t call nobody else his friend except Abraham.

“Thou whom I have taken from the ends of the earth, and called thee from the chief men thereof”: meaning he’s going to call us from all these kingdoms. “And said unto thee, Thou art my servant; I have chosen thee, and not cast thee away.”

“Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.” The right hand of his righteousness: that’s Christ. So notice what he says: fear not, I’m with you; don’t be dismayed, don’t be worried, for I’m your God. I will strengthen you, I will help you.

“Behold, all they that were incensed against thee”, all they that had hatred against us, “shall be ashamed and confounded”: those nations, those people shall be ashamed and confounded. “They shall be as nothing.” “And they that strive with thee shall perish”: all those nations, those people, those organizations that strive with us shall perish, every last one of them.

“Thou shalt seek them, and shalt not find them”: you going to look for them, but they going to be gone. Even them that fight with you: “they that war against thee shall be as nothing, and as a thing of nought.” Those nations, that people that war with us shall be as nothing.
“For I the Lord thy God will hold thy right hand”: he said, I’m going to hold your right hand, “saying unto thee, Fear not; I will help thee.”

“Fear not, thou worm Jacob”: wait, what does it call us? He calls us a worm again. We are a worm, brothers and sisters. That’s why another scripture says, where the worm dieth not: that’s your soul. “And ye men of Israel; I will help thee, saith the Lord, and thy redeemer, the Holy One of Israel.”

“Behold, I will make thee a new sharp threshing instrument”: that’s that new body. Remember we read, we get rid of this vile body and we going to have a new body, that celestial God body. “Having teeth: thou shalt thresh the mountains”: we going to thresh the governments, “and beat them small”: we going to beat them small. “And shalt make the hills as chaff”: we going to make the small countries as chaff; we going to destroy them too.

“Thou shalt fan them”: we going to fan them like you fan fire. “And the wind shall carry them away”: they going to be beat down so bad the wind going to be able to blow these nations away. “And the whirlwind shall scatter them: and thou shalt rejoice in the Lord, and shalt glory in the Holy One of Israel.” Twelve tribes, twelve tribes, twelve tribes.
